::: {.callout-warning}
The study below ran on the superseded Engine `8438ce5f` (wheel `40fba7cf`) and
its broader replay used all five reaction shifts. The selected JSON saved only
R2/R4/R5; the R1/R3 omission is a known adoption-record limitation. The
pressure rows are regenerated for the exact adopted record on the greenfield
Engine `443a9da4` (see the [overview](../notebook.qmd#pressure)); the screen,
fit and heat rows are not.
:::

# Question

Can temperature-dependent reaction corrections improve the three coupled
observables—CO₂ pressure, species distribution and absorption heat—without
reopening the EOS parameters?

# Starting point and strategy

The revised screen retained 33 targets common to all perturbations: five Jou
1995 pressure rows at 80/120 °C, 22 Böttinger 2008 speciation targets at
20–80 °C, and six Kim–Svendsen 2007 heat intervals at 40/80 °C. Xu pressure
and 120 °C heat were excluded from the fitting objective; Kim 2014 heat was a
comparison, not a fit target. Eight additional target keys were excluded when
at least one perturbation was non-evaluable.

With EOS parameters fixed, baseline and ±2.5 kJ mol⁻¹ perturbations of all five
reactions supplied finite-difference sensitivities. The fit preserved each
reaction's $\ln K$ at 313.15 K, used log-ratio residuals for pressure/speciation
and kJ mol⁻¹ CO₂ differences for heat, balanced target families and then
retained two SVD directions. Bounded least squares reached both ±5 kJ mol⁻¹
direction limits; one recenter tested the unbounded proposal through exact
Engine calculations.

::: {.parameter-table .reaction-coefficients-table}
| Reaction | Current coefficients | Adopted enthalpy shift (kJ mol⁻¹) |
|:--|:--|--:|
| R2 · CO₂ hydration | $A=232.3314$; $B=-11105.64$ K | −8.2019 |
| R4 · carbamate hydrolysis | $A=1.5050153742$; $B=-1317.0490$ K | −4.8078 |
| R5 · MEAH⁺ dissociation | $a=3037.6400$ K; $b=-1.0173151$ | +8.4185 |
:::

# Numerical result

The exact sparse weighted residual norm changed **1.0000 → 0.7530** for the
bounded fit and **0.6559** for the selected proposal. The selected sparse
RMSEs were 0.1634 for pressure, 0.0998 for speciation and 7.1813 kJ mol⁻¹
CO₂ for heat. Native R4/R5 derivatives differed from finite differences by at
most 0.22% over 45 checked rows.

::: {.parameter-table .numeric-table}
| Cohort | Paired targets | Baseline RMSE → candidate RMSE |
|:--|--:|--:|
| Pressure calibration, log₁₀ ratio | 143 | 0.3344 → 0.2366 (greenfield, adopted record: 0.2364) |
| Xu 2011 pressure comparison | 18 | 0.3096 → 0.1901 (greenfield, adopted record: 0.1910) |
| Speciation, log₁₀ ratio | 125 | 0.3702 → 0.3670 (see note) |
| Kim–Svendsen 40/80 °C heat | 66 | 20.01 → 11.84 kJ mol⁻¹ CO₂ |
| Kim–Svendsen 120 °C heat | 20 | 39.30 → 31.15 kJ mol⁻¹ CO₂ |
| Kim 2014 heat comparison | 27 | 16.84 → 10.71 kJ mol⁻¹ CO₂ |
:::

Greenfield pressure values use the same 143/18 split and differ from the
candidate replay by at most 0.009 in ln pCO₂ per row. The speciation cohort is
not re-paired here: the candidate replay returned an impossible carbamate mole
fraction of 3.53 for Böttinger 2008 state 048 through `pivot_reuse`, which
inflated both speciation values. The greenfield adopted record scores all 131
speciation targets at log₁₀ RMSE 0.2322 (overview table).

# Conclusion and limits

The two retained directions improved pressure and heat more than speciation.
Carbamate and bicarbonate partition remained poor, and the 120 °C heat bias
remained large. The paired table is candidate-replay evidence, not an exact
replay of the selected JSON because R1/R3 shifts were omitted from that
document. A selected-JSON heat replay (file `568f7a5f…`, same coefficients, superseded Engine) gives 11.8497, 31.1500 and
10.7128 kJ mol⁻¹ CO₂ for the three heat cohorts. No independent identification
of each coefficient or confidence interval was established.
